docs.text: Development For: developers of the engine. You'll find: the tests, the query catalogue and its copies, releasing, and the documentation site. The tests python -m pytest # everything REQUIRE_CASSANDRA=1 python -m pytest # fail instead of skipping without Cassandra (CI) The Cassandra tests ( tests/integration/ ) need Cassandra on 127.0.0.1:9042 , for example docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:9042:9042 cassandra:5.0.9 . For another port, set CASSANDRA_PORT=19042 . CI ( .github/workflows/ci.yml ) runs them against a real Cassandra on every push and pull request. The query catalogue and its copies The query catalogue has a query for each part of openCypher the engine supports, written against sitelabs-graph-database's sample graphs, to paste into the UI query console (sitelabs-graph-ui). tests/test_query_catalogue.py checks that every query parses, that the console's sections hold only reads, and that every parameter block is JSON. sitelabs-graph-database and sitelabs-partitioned-graph keep a copy in their docs, as it is at the tag they pin. Their tests fail if the copy is edited there, or left behind when the pin moves. Change it here, release a tag, move a project's pin, then refresh its copy: python scripts/install_catalogue.py ../sitelabs-graph-database # writes its docs/query-catalogue.md python scripts/install_catalogue.py --check ../sitelabs-partitioned-graph # is its copy current? The copy is word for word, so docs/query-catalogue.md has no menu at the top, unlike the other pages ( NO_MENU in tools/docs.py ). It names none of the projects that copy it. Releasing Add the release's entry to CHANGELOG.md (move Unreleased under the new version), and set version in pyproject.toml ( 0.3.0 ). Commit, then git tag -a v0.3.0 -m "opencypher-graphtool 0.3.0" , and push both. The tag publishes the release's documentation site. Make a GitHub release for the tag, with the entry as its notes. In each project, pin the new tag, refresh its copy of the query catalogue, and change its links to this site to the new release ( /sitelabs-opencypher-graphtool/0.3/ ). The documentation site docs/ is published at https://sitelabs-com.github.io/sitelabs-opencypher-graphtool/, one site per release, with mike : /0.2/ , /0.3/ ...: each release's site, for the engine a project pins. Projects link to these. /latest/ : the newest. The site's root sends browsers there. .github/workflows/mkdocs.yml publishes the release in pyproject.toml on every push to main that changes the docs, and on every tag. The menu at the top of each page and the sidebar come from GROUPS in tools/docs.py : python tools/docs.py # write the menus and mkdocs.yml's nav python tools/docs.py --check # change nothing; fail if a file is out of date pip install -r requirements-docs.txt mkdocs serve # the site at http://127.0.0.1:8000, as you edit mkdocs build --strict # what the workflow builds, failing on a broken link

docs.text: Extension points For: developers building on the engine. You'll find: writing a property store of your own, and changing how the runner matches patterns. Property stores The topology is in graph-tool; the properties of nodes and relationships are in a property store. The engine comes with two: Store Where the properties are InMemoryStore({}) In memory, in a dict CassandraStore(session, "keyspace") Apache Cassandra, one table per type (the cassandra extra) For another, subclass PropertyStore , from stores . A store provides the columns of a type, fetching rows by id, writing them, and, optionally, index search. InMemoryStore ( stores.py ) and CassandraStore ( cassandra_store.py ) are the examples to follow. The runner and pattern expansion OpenCypher.runner is the class that runs a query: the _Run of clauses . A subclass can override its matching steps, defined in matching : Step What it does seed(labels, eqs) A pattern's start nodes: the candidates for an unbound node, by id, store index, label mask or scan filter_nodes(cands, labels, eqs) Keeps the candidates having all labels and every equality, batching store reads choose_start(part, bound, hints) Which node of a pattern part to start matching from neighbourhood(nodes, direction, types, labels) The hook before the matcher reads incident relationships The matcher calls neighbourhood : once per hop, with the whole frontier; once per level of a variable-length pattern; once per BFS layer of shortestPath() ; in degree() . On a local graph it does nothing. sitelabs-partitioned-graph uses it to fetch each hop from the partitions that own the nodes.

docs.text: The modules For: developers of the engine, and anyone reading its code. You'll find: each module of the package, in the order they load, and how they import each other. The engine was one 6,400-line module ( opencypher_gt ). It is now a package of modules, src/opencypher_graphtool/ , listed here in the order they load: Module What errors The exceptions ( OpenCypherError , ConstraintError , lock errors, ...) locking One fair readers-writer lock per graph ( GraphLock , lock_of ) common The write transaction record, sentinels, core keys ids Element ids: UUIDs, natural-key ids ( bulk_node_id , stable_id ) lexer , ast_nodes , parser openCypher text to a syntax tree ( parse ) values Values, null logic, ordering, the built-in functions results Node , Rel , Path , Result models The data model: Models , NodeModel , RelationshipModel , Field , Vector , migrations schema Labels and types as bitmasks, UUID ids, attached to a graph-tool Graph elements Creating, changing and deleting nodes and relationships, with undo for transactions stores The property store interface ( PropertyStore ) and InMemoryStore cassandra_store CassandraStore (the cassandra extra) execution , graph_functions , matching , clauses The query runner, built up module by module: core, graph functions, MATCH (pattern expansion), the clauses procedures CALL procedures (PageRank, components, shortest paths, vector.search , ...) engine OpenCypher , opencypher() , VerifyReport How the modules import each other Each module imports what it needs from the modules before it, at the top. The few names it needs from the modules after it are bound by its _link() function, which the package's __init__ calls once every module is loaded. Import the public API from the package ( from opencypher_graphtool import ... ). Importing a module directly works too, since the package loads first. The public API The public API is what opencypher_graphtool exports ( OpenCypher , the models and fields, Schema , the stores, the errors), the openCypher the engine accepts, and the tables and ids it writes: what a stored graph or keyspace needs to keep working. A change to any of these is a Changed entry in CHANGELOG.md .

docs.text: Overview For: developers using the engine in a project, and developers of it. You'll find: what the engine is, who uses it, installing it, a first query, and its versions. opencypher_graphtool is an openCypher query engine for graph-tool graphs. The topology lives in graph-tool, in memory. Node and relationship properties live in a pluggable property store: in memory, or Apache Cassandra (one table per type). A pydantic data model is the single source of truth for types, labels, tables and validation. It is the engine shared by: sitelabs-graph-database : the graph database (write server, read replicas, failover, Cassandra), and sitelabs-partitioned-graph : an in-memory graph partitioned over many servers. This site describes the engine itself. Each project's own documentation says how it serves the engine: its endpoints, its console, its deployment, and what of openCypher it doesn't support. What's where Part In short Page The modules The package, module by module, and how they import each other The modules Extension points Property stores of your own, and the runner's matching steps Extension points The language, by example A query for each part of openCypher the engine supports Query catalogue Development The tests, the catalogue's copies, releasing, this site Development Installing graph-tool is not on PyPI: it comes from conda-forge, so the engine is installed into a conda environment that already has it. conda env create -f environment.yml # python, graph-tool, then this package (editable) conda activate opencypher-graphtool python -m pytest # the tests (Cassandra ones skip without it) In another project, with graph-tool in its environment: pip install -e ../sitelabs-opencypher-graphtool[cassandra] # while developing both side by side pip install "opencypher-graphtool[cassandra] @ git+https://github.com/sitelabs-com/sitelabs-opencypher-graphtool.git@v0.2.0" The cassandra extra adds the Cassandra driver (for CassandraStore ). Without it the engine runs on InMemoryStore or a store of your own. A first query from graph_tool import Graph from opencypher_graphtool import RelationshipModel, Field, InMemoryStore, Models, NodeModel, opencypher class Person(NodeModel): class Meta: type = "Person" name: str = Field(index=True) class Knows(RelationshipModel): class Meta: type = "KNOWS" source, target = "Person", "Person" # descriptive since: int | None = None cy = opencypher(Graph(), InMemoryStore({}), models=Models([Person, Knows])) cy.run("CREATE (:Person {name: 'Ann'})-[:KNOWS {since: 2020}]->(:Person {name: 'Bob'})") print(cy.run("MATCH (a:Person)-[k:KNOWS]->(b) RETURN a.name AS a, b.name AS b, k.since AS s").data()) With Cassandra, use CassandraStore(session, "keyspace") instead of InMemoryStore({}) . There are more examples in examples/ . Versions Releases are git tags ( v0.1.0 , ...), each with an entry in CHANGELOG.md : what changed, and under Upgrading what to do. Before 1.0, a minor release (0.1 to 0.2) may change the public API; a patch release doesn't. The projects using the engine pin a tag in their requirements, and move to a new one deliberately. This site has one version per release ( /0.2/ , ...), and /latest/ : a project links to the release it pins. 0.2.0 names graph elements nodes and relationships everywhere, as openCypher does, not vertices and edges (graph-tool's own API, underneath, keeps its names). It changes the API: Was Now VertexModel , EdgeModel NodeModel , RelationshipModel Schema(vertex_labels=, vertex_types=, edge_types=) , reg("vertex", ...) Schema(node_labels=, node_types=, relationship_types=) , reg("node", ...) The kinds "vertex" , "edge" ( table_namer(kind, type) , stores, models) "node" , "relationship" reverse_vertex_ids (the default reverse id table) reverse_node_ids What was stored before still works: graphs saved with the old schema keys load, a keyspace that already has reverse_vertex_ids keeps using it, and a MERGE or a file import makes the same ids as before ( tests/test_compatibility.py ).

docs.text: openCypher query catalogue For: anyone trying the engine's openCypher in the UI query console (sitelabs-graph-ui). You'll find: one or more queries for each part of the language the engine supports, ready to copy into the console's query box, and what each one shows. Every query below runs as written against two sample graphs, a karate club and a citation graph (two return no rows on purpose, and say so). Where the project serving the console ships them, load them once, from its directory: python -m example_solutions.example_graphs.karate_club # 34 :Member nodes, 78 :FRIENDS_WITH relationships python -m example_solutions.example_graphs.citations # 48 :Document nodes (with embeddings), 77 :CITES relationships Karate club: (:Member {member_no, name, role, faction})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->(:Member) . Member 1 is "Mr. Hi", member 34 is "John A.". Each friendship is stored once, lower member_no to higher, so most queries match it in either direction: -[:FRIENDS_WITH]- . Citations: (:Document {title, topic, year, embedding})-[:CITES]->(:Document) . Four topics, 12 papers each, from 2015 to 2026. embedding is a 16-number vector. Parameters. A query that uses $name has its parameters in a JSON block under it: paste that into the console's parameters box. Writes. The console is read-only and refuses any query that would change the graph. The queries in Writes are for POST /opencypher ; in the console, press Explain on them to see their plan without running them. What the engine does not support is listed in the documentation of the project serving the console. Catalogue procedures Literals Operators Null and three-valued logic Lists Maps CASE Functions MATCH and patterns Variable-length patterns and paths Shortest paths OPTIONAL MATCH Pattern predicates, EXISTS and pattern comprehensions WITH RETURN, ORDER BY, SKIP and LIMIT Aggregation UNWIND UNION Parameters Graph functions Graph algorithm procedures Vector search EXPLAIN Writes Catalogue procedures The labels, relationship types and property keys in the graph: CALL db.labels() YIELD label RETURN label CALL db.relationshipTypes() YIELD relationshipType RETURN relationshipType CALL db.propertyKeys() YIELD propertyKey RETURN propertyKey ORDER BY propertyKey Literals Numbers: integers, hexadecimal, floats, exponents and negatives: RETURN 42 AS int, 0x1F AS hex, 3.14 AS float, 6.02e23 AS exponent, 1e-3 AS small, -7 AS negative Strings in single or double quotes, with escapes ( \' , \" , \n , \t , \\ , \uXXXX ): RETURN 'single' AS a, "double" AS b, 'it\'s' AS c, "say \"hi\"" AS d, 'tab:\there' AS e, 'café' AS f Booleans, null, lists and maps, nested: RETURN true AS t, false AS f, null AS n, [1, 'two', 3.0, [4]] AS list, {name: 'Ann', tags: ['a', 'b'], address: {city: 'Sydney'}} AS map Comments, and backtick-quoted names (with spaces, or that would be keywords): // a line comment MATCH (`the member`:Member) /* a block comment */ WHERE `the member`.member_no = 1 RETURN `the member`.name AS `Member name`, 1 AS `match` Operators Arithmetic: + - * / % ^ and unary minus. Integer division truncates; ^ always gives a float: RETURN 7 + 2 AS add, 7 - 2 AS sub, 7 * 2 AS mul, 7 / 2 AS int_div, 7.0 / 2 AS float_div, 7 % 2 AS mod, 2 ^ 10 AS pow, -(3 + 4) AS neg Precedence and parentheses: RETURN 2 + 3 * 4 AS a, (2 + 3) * 4 AS b, -2 ^ 2 AS c, 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 AS right_assoc + joins strings and lists too: RETURN 'graph' + '-' + 'tool' AS s, [1, 2] + [3] AS l, [1, 2] + 3 AS l2 Comparisons, including chained ones ( a < b <= c means a < b AND b <= c ): RETURN 1 = 1 AS eq, 1 <> 2 AS ne, 1 != 2 AS ne2, 1 < 2 AS lt, 2 <= 2 AS le, 3 > 2 AS gt, 3 >= 4 AS ge, 1 < 2 <= 2 < 3 AS chained, 'a' < 'b' AS strings Boolean operators: RETURN true AND false AS and_, true OR false AS or_, true XOR true AS xor_, NOT false AS not_ String operators: STARTS WITH , ENDS WITH , CONTAINS and regular expressions ( =~ , the whole string must match): MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.name STARTS WITH 'Member 2' OR m.name ENDS WITH '.' OR m.name CONTAINS 'Hi' RETURN m.member_no, m.name ORDER BY m.member_no MATCH (d:Document) WHERE d.title =~ '(?i)quorum.*' RETURN d.title, d.year IN a list: MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.member_no IN [1, 2, 33, 34] RETURN m.member_no, m.name, m.role Null and three-valued logic null propagates through comparisons and arithmetic, and AND / OR follow three-valued logic: RETURN null = null AS eq, null <> 1 AS ne, null + 1 AS plus, null OR true AS or_true, null OR false AS or_false, null AND false AS and_false, NOT null AS not_null IN with a null in the list, and IS NULL / IS NOT NULL : RETURN 2 IN [1, 2, null] AS found, 3 IN [1, 2, null] AS unknown, null IS NULL AS a, 1 IS NOT NULL AS b A missing property is null: MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) RETURN m.nickname AS missing, m.nickname IS NULL AS is_null, coalesce(m.nickname, m.name) AS shown Lists Indexing (negative counts from the end) and slicing ( [from..to] , to exclusive, either may be left out): WITH [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] AS l RETURN l[0] AS first, l[-1] AS last, l[1..3] AS middle, l[..2] AS head2, l[-2..] AS tail2, l[10] AS out_of_range List comprehensions: filter, map, or both: WITH range(1, 10) AS l RETURN [x IN l WHERE x % 2 = 0] AS evens, [x IN l | x * x] AS squares, [x IN l WHERE x > 7 | x * 10] AS both Quantifiers all , any , none , single : WITH [2, 4, 6, 7] AS l RETURN all(x IN l WHERE x > 0) AS all_pos, any(x IN l WHERE x % 2 = 1) AS any_odd, none(x IN l WHERE x > 100) AS none_big, single(x IN l WHERE x = 7) AS one_seven reduce : RETURN reduce(total = 0, x IN range(1, 100) | total + x) AS sum_1_to_100, reduce(s = '', w IN ['a', 'b', 'c'] | s + w) AS joined List functions: RETURN range(0, 10, 3) AS stepped, range(5, 1, -2) AS down, size([1, 2, 3]) AS size, head([1, 2, 3]) AS head, last([1, 2, 3]) AS last, tail([1, 2, 3]) AS tail, reverse([1, 2, 3]) AS reversed, isEmpty([]) AS empty Lists from the graph, compared with comprehensions over them: MATCH (d:Document {topic: 'query languages'}) WITH collect(d.year) AS years RETURN years, [y IN years WHERE y >= 2022] AS recent, size(years) AS n Maps Keys by .name or ['name'] , nested access, and keys() : WITH {name: 'Ann', tags: ['a', 'b'], address: {city: 'Sydney'}} AS m RETURN m.name AS name, m['tags'][1] AS second_tag, m.address.city AS city, keys(m) AS keys A property chosen at run time, with n[expression] : MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) RETURN m[$key] AS value, m['role'] AS role {"key": "faction"} Building a map from a node (the engine has no map projection n{.a, .b} , so write the map out): MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.member_no <= 3 RETURN {no: m.member_no, name: m.name, faction: m.faction} AS member, properties(m) AS all_properties CASE The generic form (conditions): MATCH (d:Document) RETURN d.title, CASE WHEN d.year < 2018 THEN 'early' WHEN d.year < 2023 THEN 'middle' ELSE 'recent' END AS era ORDER BY d.year LIMIT 10 The simple form (one value against several): MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no, CASE m.role WHEN 'instructor' THEN 'teaches' WHEN 'administrator' THEN 'runs the club' ELSE 'trains' END AS does ORDER BY m.member_no LIMIT 5 Functions Strings: RETURN toUpper('graph') AS up, toLower('GRAPH') AS low, trim(' x ') AS trim, ltrim(' x') AS ltrim, rtrim('x ') AS rtrim, replace('a-b-c', '-', '+') AS replace, substring('openCypher', 4) AS sub, substring('openCypher', 0, 4) AS sub2, left('openCypher', 4) AS left, right('openCypher', 6) AS right, split('a,b,c', ',') AS split, reverse('abc') AS rev, size('hello') AS size Numbers: RETURN abs(-3) AS abs, ceil(1.2) AS ceil, floor(1.8) AS floor, round(2.5) AS round, round(3.14159, 2) AS round2, round(2.5, 0, 'HALF_EVEN') AS banker, sign(-4) AS sign, sqrt(16) AS sqrt, exp(1) AS exp, log(e()) AS log, log10(1000) AS log10 Trigonometry and constants: RETURN pi() AS pi, e() AS e, sin(pi() / 2) AS sin, cos(0) AS cos, tan(0) AS tan, asin(1) AS asin, acos(1) AS acos, atan(1) AS atan, atan2(1, 1) AS atan2, degrees(pi()) AS degrees, radians(180) AS radians Conversions: RETURN toInteger('42') AS i, toInteger(3.9) AS trunc, toFloat('2.5') AS f, toBoolean('true') AS b, toString(12) AS s, toString(true) AS s2, toInteger('nope') AS bad Others: coalesce , timestamp (milliseconds since 1970), randomUUID and rand (0 to 1): RETURN coalesce(null, null, 'third') AS first_non_null, timestamp() AS now_ms, randomUUID() AS uuid, rand() AS random MATCH and patterns All nodes with a label, and inline property maps: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m ORDER BY m.member_no LIMIT 5 MATCH (m:Member {faction: 'Officer', role: 'member'}) RETURN m.member_no, m.name ORDER BY m.member_no Any node, with a label test in WHERE : MATCH (n) WHERE n:Document AND n.year = 2015 RETURN labels(n) AS labels, n.title Several labels at once ( :A:B ): no sample node has two, so this returns nothing, but it shows the syntax in both places: MATCH (n:Member:Person) RETURN n UNION MATCH (n) WHERE n:Member:Document RETURN n Relationship directions: outgoing, incoming, either way, and anonymous relationships: MATCH (d:Document {title: 'Pattern matching, part 2'})-[:CITES]->(cited) RETURN 'cites' AS dir, cited.title AS title UNION ALL MATCH (d:Document {title: 'Pattern matching, part 2'})<-[:CITES]-(citing) RETURN 'cited by' AS dir, citing.title AS title MATCH (:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(friend) RETURN friend.member_no ORDER BY friend.member_no MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 34})--(b) RETURN count(b) AS either, size([(a)-->(x) | x]) AS out, size([(a)<--(x) | x]) AS in A relationship variable, its type and properties, and type alternatives [:A|B] : MATCH (a)-[r:FRIENDS_WITH|CITES]->(b) RETURN type(r) AS type, count(*) AS n MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[r:FRIENDS_WITH]->(b) RETURN r, startNode(r).name AS from, endNode(r).name AS to LIMIT 3 Longer chains: friends of friends that are not direct friends: MATCH (me:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(fof) WHERE fof <> me AND NOT (me)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(fof) RETURN DISTINCT fof.member_no AS suggestion ORDER BY suggestion Cycles: every friendship triangle, each once: MATCH (a:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(b:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(c:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(a) WHERE a.member_no < b.member_no < c.member_no RETURN a.member_no, b.member_no, c.member_no ORDER BY a.member_no, b.member_no, c.member_no Several pattern parts separated by commas, sharing a node: MATCH (hi:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(x), (x)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(john:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN x.member_no AS friend_of_both, x.faction Several MATCH clauses in a row: MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1}) MATCH (b:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN a.name, b.name, (a)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(b) AS are_friends Variable-length patterns and paths Exactly 2 hops ( *2 ), a range ( *1..2 ), at most ( *..2 ), and at least ( *2.. , capped by the server): MATCH (:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*2]-(m) RETURN DISTINCT m.member_no ORDER BY m.member_no MATCH (:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*1..2]-(m) RETURN count(DISTINCT m) AS within_two_hops MATCH (:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*..2]-(m) RETURN count(DISTINCT m) AS within_two_hops MATCH (d:Document {title: 'Variable-length paths, part 2'})-[:CITES*3..]->(old) RETURN DISTINCT old.title, old.year ORDER BY old.year LIMIT 5 Any number of hops ( * ) along the citations, with a path variable, and the path functions: MATCH p = (d:Document {title: 'Variable-length paths, part 2'})-[:CITES*]->(old:Document {year: 2015}) RETURN p, length(p) AS hops, [n IN nodes(p) | n.year] AS years, [r IN relationships(p) | type(r)] AS types ORDER BY hops LIMIT 3 A path variable on a fixed-length pattern, and a relationship-list variable on a variable-length one: MATCH p = (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->(b)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->(c) RETURN p, length(p) AS len LIMIT 5 MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[rs:FRIENDS_WITH*2]-(c:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN [r IN rs | [startNode(r).member_no, endNode(r).member_no]] AS steps Shortest paths shortestPath() (one) and allShortestPaths() (every one of the shortest length): MATCH p = shortestPath((a:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*]-(b:Member {member_no: 26})) RETURN p, length(p) AS hops, [n IN nodes(p) | n.member_no] AS via MATCH p = allShortestPaths((a:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*]-(b:Member {member_no: 26})) RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.member_no] AS via ORDER BY via With a hop limit, and following direction: MATCH p = shortestPath((a:Document {title: 'Variable-length paths, part 2'})-[:CITES*..10]->(b:Document {year: 2015})) RETURN b.title, length(p) AS hops ORDER BY hops, b.title OPTIONAL MATCH Keeps the row, with nulls, when the pattern isn't found: the first paper cites nothing: MATCH (d:Document) WHERE d.year <= 2016 OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:CITES]->(c:Document) RETURN d.title, d.year, count(c) AS cites, collect(c.title) AS titles ORDER BY d.year, d.title MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 12}) OPTIONAL MATCH (m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f:Member) WHERE f.member_no > 1 RETURN m.member_no, f.member_no AS other_friend Pattern predicates, EXISTS and pattern comprehensions A pattern as a condition, and its negation: MATCH (m:Member) WHERE (m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(:Member {member_no: 1}) AND (m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN m.member_no AS friend_of_both_leaders MATCH (d:Document) WHERE NOT (d)<-[:CITES]-() RETURN d.title AS never_cited, d.year ORDER BY d.year DESC LIMIT 10 EXISTS { pattern } , with or without a WHERE : MATCH (d:Document) WHERE EXISTS { (d)-[:CITES]->(other:Document) WHERE other.topic <> d.topic } RETURN d.title AS cites_another_topic, d.topic ORDER BY d.title Pattern comprehensions: a list built from a pattern, per row: MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.member_no IN [1, 34] RETURN m.name, [(m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WHERE f.faction <> m.faction | f.member_no] AS friends_across_the_split Counting with one (the engine has no COUNT { } subquery): MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no, size([(m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) | f]) AS friends ORDER BY friends DESC LIMIT 5 WITH Passing values on, filtering after an aggregate (like SQL's HAVING ): MATCH (m:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WITH m, count(f) AS friends WHERE friends >= 10 RETURN m.member_no, m.name, friends ORDER BY friends DESC ORDER BY and LIMIT inside WITH , before matching on: MATCH (d:Document) WITH d ORDER BY d.year DESC, d.title LIMIT 1 MATCH (d)-[:CITES]->(c) RETURN d.title AS newest, collect(c.title) AS it_cites WITH DISTINCT , and WITH * (keep every variable, add more): MATCH (d:Document) WITH DISTINCT d.topic AS topic RETURN topic ORDER BY topic MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(b) WITH *, b.member_no * 10 AS score RETURN a.member_no, b.member_no, score ORDER BY score LIMIT 3 Chaining several WITH stages: MATCH (d:Document) WITH d.topic AS topic, min(d.year) AS first, max(d.year) AS last WITH topic, last - first AS span WHERE span > 5 RETURN topic, span ORDER BY topic RETURN, ORDER BY, SKIP and LIMIT RETURN * , RETURN DISTINCT , aliases, expressions: MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN * MATCH (m:Member) RETURN DISTINCT m.faction AS faction, m.role AS role ORDER BY faction, role Several sort keys, ascending and descending ( ASC , ASCENDING , DESC , DESCENDING ): MATCH (d:Document) RETURN d.topic, d.year, d.title ORDER BY d.topic ASCENDING, d.year DESC LIMIT 8 Paging with SKIP and LIMIT , including expressions: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no ORDER BY m.member_no SKIP 10 LIMIT 5 MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no ORDER BY m.member_no SKIP $page * $size LIMIT $size {"page": 2, "size": 5} Nulls sort last when ascending (first when descending): UNWIND [3, null, 1, 2] AS x RETURN x ORDER BY x Aggregation count(*) , count(expr) (skips nulls), count(DISTINCT ...) ; the other columns are the grouping keys: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.faction AS faction, count(*) AS members, count(DISTINCT m.role) AS roles ORDER BY faction UNWIND [1, null, 2, 2] AS x RETURN count(*) AS rows, count(x) AS values, count(DISTINCT x) AS distinct_values sum , avg , min , max : MATCH (d:Document) RETURN d.topic, sum(d.year) AS sum, avg(d.year) AS avg, min(d.year) AS min, max(d.title) AS last_title ORDER BY d.topic collect and collect(DISTINCT ...) : MATCH (m:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WHERE m.member_no IN [1, 34] RETURN m.name, collect(f.member_no) AS friends, collect(DISTINCT f.faction) AS factions Statistics: stDev (sample), stDevP (population), percentileCont (interpolated), percentileDisc (an actual value): MATCH (m:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WITH m, count(f) AS degree RETURN stDev(degree) AS stdev, stDevP(degree) AS stdevp, percentileCont(degree, 0.5) AS median, percentileDisc(degree, 0.9) AS p90, avg(degree) AS mean Aggregates inside expressions, and aggregating a whole graph to one row: MATCH (d:Document) RETURN count(*) AS papers, max(d.year) - min(d.year) + 1 AS years, round(toFloat(count(*)) / 4, 1) AS per_topic UNWIND A list into rows, nested UNWIND s, and range() : UNWIND ['a', 'b'] AS letter UNWIND range(1, 3) AS n RETURN letter + toString(n) AS cell From a parameter, then matching on each value: UNWIND $members AS no MATCH (m:Member {member_no: no}) RETURN no, m.name, m.faction {"members": [1, 9, 34]} A collected list back into rows: MATCH (d:Document {topic: 'vector retrieval'}) WITH collect(d) AS docs UNWIND docs[0..3] AS d RETURN d.title An empty list gives no rows: UNWIND [] AS x RETURN x UNION UNION removes duplicate rows, UNION ALL keeps them; the column names must match: MATCH (m:Member {role: 'instructor'}) RETURN m.name AS name UNION MATCH (m:Member {role: 'administrator'}) RETURN m.name AS name UNION MATCH (m:Member {role: 'instructor'}) RETURN m.name AS name RETURN 1 AS x UNION ALL RETURN 1 AS x UNION ALL RETURN 2 AS x Parameters Values of every JSON type, used in a pattern and in expressions: MATCH (m:Member {faction: $faction}) WHERE m.member_no IN $numbers AND m.name STARTS WITH $prefix RETURN m.member_no, m.name, $flag AS flag, $settings.colour AS colour {"faction": "Mr. Hi", "numbers": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 20], "prefix": "Member", "flag": true, "settings": {"colour": "blue"}} Finding a node by its id, as the console's Expand neighbours does (take an id from any answer): MATCH (a)-[r]-(b) WHERE id(a) = $id RETURN a, r, b {"id": "paste an id here"} Graph functions A node's id, labels, keys and properties, and a relationship's type and ends: MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[r:FRIENDS_WITH]->(b:Member {member_no: 2}) RETURN id(a) AS id, elementId(a) AS element_id, labels(a) AS labels, keys(a) AS keys, properties(a) AS props, type(r) AS type, id(startNode(r)) = id(a) AS starts_at_a, endNode(r).name AS ends_at degree() : all relationships, or one direction only: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no, degree(m) AS all, degree(m, 'out') AS out, degree(m, 'in') AS in ORDER BY all DESC LIMIT 5 exists(property) (from older openCypher; IS NOT NULL is the modern form): MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) RETURN exists(m.name) AS has_name, exists(m.nickname) AS has_nickname length() of a path and size() of a list or string: MATCH p = (:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->()-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->() RETURN length(p) AS path, size(nodes(p)) AS nodes, size('abc') AS string LIMIT 1 Graph algorithm procedures These run in graph-tool over the whole graph. YIELD names the columns, AS renames them, and a WHERE after YIELD filters them. PageRank, on the friendships only, both directions: CALL gt.pageRank({direction: 'BOTH', relationshipTypes: ['FRIENDS_WITH'], dampingFactor: 0.85}) YIELD node, score AS rank WHERE node:Member RETURN node.member_no, node.name, round(rank, 4) AS rank ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT 5 The most cited papers by PageRank (direction follows the citations): CALL gt.pageRank({relationshipTypes: ['CITES'], maxIterations: 100, tolerance: 0.000001}) YIELD node, score WHERE node:Document RETURN node.title, node.year, round(score, 4) AS score ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 5 Connected components: CALL gt.connectedComponents() YIELD node, componentId RETURN componentId, labels(node)[0] AS label, count(*) AS size ORDER BY size DESC Label propagation ( gt.peerPressure ), its clusters set against the club's two factions: CALL gt.peerPressure({relationshipTypes: ['FRIENDS_WITH'], maxIterations: 30}) YIELD node, cluster WITH node, cluster WHERE node:Member RETURN cluster, node.faction AS faction, count(*) AS members ORDER BY cluster, faction A shortest path from a procedure, with matched nodes as its arguments: MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 17}), (b:Member {member_no: 26}) CALL gt.shortestPath(a, b, {direction: 'BOTH', relationshipTypes: ['FRIENDS_WITH']}) YIELD path, totalCost RETURN path, totalCost, [n IN nodes(path) | n.member_no] AS via Vector search The parameter q is a 16-number stand-in for the embedding of a question about vector retrieval (the centre of the sample's "vector retrieval" topic); it is the same under each query here. The k most similar papers (a nearest-neighbour search in Cassandra): CALL vector.search('Document', 'embedding', $q, 5) YIELD node, score RETURN node.title AS title, node.topic AS topic, round(score, 4) AS score {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} With a filter on an indexed field, applied inside Cassandra: CALL vector.search('Document', 'embedding', $q, 3, {topic: 'query languages'}) YIELD node, score RETURN node.title AS title, round(score, 4) AS score {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} Vector search, then the graph: what the best matches cite: CALL vector.search('Document', 'embedding', $q, 3) YIELD node, score MATCH (node)-[:CITES*1..2]->(src:Document) RETURN src.title AS cited, max(round(score, 4)) AS relevance ORDER BY relevance DESC, cited LIMIT 5 {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} The graph, then similarity: the similarity functions score vectors already in hand ( vector.cosine , vector.dot_product , vector.euclidean , each from 0 to 1): MATCH (d:Document) WITH d ORDER BY d.year DESC LIMIT 1 MATCH (d)-[:CITES*1..3]->(c:Document) RETURN DISTINCT c.title AS title, round(vector.cosine(c.embedding, $q), 4) AS cosine, round(vector.dot_product(c.embedding, $q), 4) AS dot, round(vector.euclidean(c.embedding, $q), 4) AS euclidean ORDER BY cosine DESC LIMIT 5 {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} Two papers compared with each other: MATCH (a:Document {title: 'Leader leases, part 1'}), (b:Document) WHERE b <> a RETURN b.title, b.topic, round(vector.cosine(a.embedding, b.embedding), 4) AS similarity ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT 5 EXPLAIN The plan, not the answer: where each pattern starts and how its start nodes are found. The console's Explain button adds the EXPLAIN for you. EXPLAIN MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) RETURN f.name EXPLAIN of a write is a read, so the console accepts it: EXPLAIN MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) SET m.role = 'instructor' RETURN m Writes Not in the console , which refuses writes: send these to POST /opencypher with a key that may write, for example curl -s -X POST 127.0.0.1:5050/opencypher -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query": "CREATE (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p", "params": {"name": "Catalogue Ann"}}' They use the data model's Person / KNOWS types, with names starting Catalogue , and run in order; the last one removes everything they made. In the console, Explain shows each one's plan. CREATE : a node, a path, and a relationship between nodes already there: CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann', address: '1 First St'}) RETURN p CREATE (b:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'})-[k:KNOWS {since: 2020}]->(c:Person {name: 'Catalogue Cat'}) RETURN b, k, c MATCH (a:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}), (b:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'}) CREATE (a)-[k:KNOWS {since: 2015}]->(b) RETURN a, k, b MERGE : find or create, with ON CREATE SET and ON MATCH SET (run it twice to see both): MERGE (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Dan'}) ON CREATE SET p.address = 'created' ON MATCH SET p.address = 'matched' RETURN p.name, p.address MATCH (a:Person {name: 'Catalogue Dan'}), (b:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) MERGE (a)-[k:KNOWS]->(b) ON CREATE SET k.since = 2024 RETURN k.since Many at once, from a parameter: UNWIND $people AS person MERGE (p:Person {name: person.name}) SET p.address = person.address RETURN count(p) AS merged {"people": [{"name": "Catalogue Eve", "address": "5 Fifth St"}, {"name": "Catalogue Fay", "address": "6 Sixth St"}]} SET : one property, several properties from a map ( += adds, = replaces them all), and a label: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) SET p.address = '2 Second St' RETURN p MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'}) SET p += {address: '3 Third St'} RETURN properties(p) MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Cat'}) SET p = {name: 'Catalogue Cat', address: '4 Fourth St'} RETURN properties(p) MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) SET p:Member RETURN labels(p) REMOVE : a property and a label: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) REMOVE p.address, p:Member RETURN p.address, labels(p) DELETE a relationship, then DETACH DELETE the nodes with their relationships: MATCH (:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'})-[k:KNOWS]->(:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'}) DELETE k MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name STARTS WITH 'Catalogue' DETACH DELETE p

docs.text: For: anyone trying the engine's openCypher in the UI query console (sitelabs-graph-ui). You'll find: one or more queries for each part of the language the engine supports, ready to copy into the console's query box, and what each one shows. Every query below runs as written against two sample graphs, a karate club and a citation graph (two return no rows on purpose, and say so). Where the project serving the console ships them, load them once, from its directory: python -m example_solutions.example_graphs.karate_club # 34 :Member nodes, 78 :FRIENDS_WITH relationships python -m example_solutions.example_graphs.citations # 48 :Document nodes (with embeddings), 77 :CITES relationships Karate club: (:Member {member_no, name, role, faction})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->(:Member) . Member 1 is "Mr. Hi", member 34 is "John A.". Each friendship is stored once, lower member_no to higher, so most queries match it in either direction: -[:FRIENDS_WITH]- . Citations: (:Document {title, topic, year, embedding})-[:CITES]->(:Document) . Four topics, 12 papers each, from 2015 to 2026. embedding is a 16-number vector. Parameters. A query that uses $name has its parameters in a JSON block under it: paste that into the console's parameters box. Writes. The console is read-only and refuses any query that would change the graph. The queries in Writes are for POST /opencypher ; in the console, press Explain on them to see their plan without running them. What the engine does not support is listed in the documentation of the project serving the console. docs.text: Numbers: integers, hexadecimal, floats, exponents and negatives: RETURN 42 AS int, 0x1F AS hex, 3.14 AS float, 6.02e23 AS exponent, 1e-3 AS small, -7 AS negative Strings in single or double quotes, with escapes ( \' , \" , \n , \t , \\ , \uXXXX ): RETURN 'single' AS a, "double" AS b, 'it\'s' AS c, "say \"hi\"" AS d, 'tab:\there' AS e, 'café' AS f Booleans, null, lists and maps, nested: RETURN true AS t, false AS f, null AS n, [1, 'two', 3.0, [4]] AS list, {name: 'Ann', tags: ['a', 'b'], address: {city: 'Sydney'}} AS map Comments, and backtick-quoted names (with spaces, or that would be keywords): // a line comment MATCH (`the member`:Member) /* a block comment */ WHERE `the member`.member_no = 1 RETURN `the member`.name AS `Member name`, 1 AS `match`

docs.text: Arithmetic: + - * / % ^ and unary minus. Integer division truncates; ^ always gives a float: RETURN 7 + 2 AS add, 7 - 2 AS sub, 7 * 2 AS mul, 7 / 2 AS int_div, 7.0 / 2 AS float_div, 7 % 2 AS mod, 2 ^ 10 AS pow, -(3 + 4) AS neg Precedence and parentheses: RETURN 2 + 3 * 4 AS a, (2 + 3) * 4 AS b, -2 ^ 2 AS c, 2 ^ 3 ^ 2 AS right_assoc + joins strings and lists too: RETURN 'graph' + '-' + 'tool' AS s, [1, 2] + [3] AS l, [1, 2] + 3 AS l2 Comparisons, including chained ones ( a < b <= c means a < b AND b <= c ): RETURN 1 = 1 AS eq, 1 <> 2 AS ne, 1 != 2 AS ne2, 1 < 2 AS lt, 2 <= 2 AS le, 3 > 2 AS gt, 3 >= 4 AS ge, 1 < 2 <= 2 < 3 AS chained, 'a' < 'b' AS strings Boolean operators: RETURN true AND false AS and_, true OR false AS or_, true XOR true AS xor_, NOT false AS not_ String operators: STARTS WITH , ENDS WITH , CONTAINS and regular expressions ( =~ , the whole string must match): MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.name STARTS WITH 'Member 2' OR m.name ENDS WITH '.' OR m.name CONTAINS 'Hi' RETURN m.member_no, m.name ORDER BY m.member_no MATCH (d:Document) WHERE d.title =~ '(?i)quorum.*' RETURN d.title, d.year IN a list: MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.member_no IN [1, 2, 33, 34] RETURN m.member_no, m.name, m.role
docs.title: Operators

docs.text: null propagates through comparisons and arithmetic, and AND / OR follow three-valued logic: RETURN null = null AS eq, null <> 1 AS ne, null + 1 AS plus, null OR true AS or_true, null OR false AS or_false, null AND false AS and_false, NOT null AS not_null IN with a null in the list, and IS NULL / IS NOT NULL : RETURN 2 IN [1, 2, null] AS found, 3 IN [1, 2, null] AS unknown, null IS NULL AS a, 1 IS NOT NULL AS b A missing property is null: MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) RETURN m.nickname AS missing, m.nickname IS NULL AS is_null, coalesce(m.nickname, m.name) AS shown
docs.title: Null and three-valued logic

docs.text: Indexing (negative counts from the end) and slicing ( [from..to] , to exclusive, either may be left out): WITH [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] AS l RETURN l[0] AS first, l[-1] AS last, l[1..3] AS middle, l[..2] AS head2, l[-2..] AS tail2, l[10] AS out_of_range List comprehensions: filter, map, or both: WITH range(1, 10) AS l RETURN [x IN l WHERE x % 2 = 0] AS evens, [x IN l | x * x] AS squares, [x IN l WHERE x > 7 | x * 10] AS both Quantifiers all , any , none , single : WITH [2, 4, 6, 7] AS l RETURN all(x IN l WHERE x > 0) AS all_pos, any(x IN l WHERE x % 2 = 1) AS any_odd, none(x IN l WHERE x > 100) AS none_big, single(x IN l WHERE x = 7) AS one_seven reduce : RETURN reduce(total = 0, x IN range(1, 100) | total + x) AS sum_1_to_100, reduce(s = '', w IN ['a', 'b', 'c'] | s + w) AS joined List functions: RETURN range(0, 10, 3) AS stepped, range(5, 1, -2) AS down, size([1, 2, 3]) AS size, head([1, 2, 3]) AS head, last([1, 2, 3]) AS last, tail([1, 2, 3]) AS tail, reverse([1, 2, 3]) AS reversed, isEmpty([]) AS empty Lists from the graph, compared with comprehensions over them: MATCH (d:Document {topic: 'query languages'}) WITH collect(d.year) AS years RETURN years, [y IN years WHERE y >= 2022] AS recent, size(years) AS n
docs.title: Lists

docs.text: Keys by .name or ['name'] , nested access, and keys() : WITH {name: 'Ann', tags: ['a', 'b'], address: {city: 'Sydney'}} AS m RETURN m.name AS name, m['tags'][1] AS second_tag, m.address.city AS city, keys(m) AS keys A property chosen at run time, with n[expression] : MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) RETURN m[$key] AS value, m['role'] AS role {"key": "faction"} Building a map from a node (the engine has no map projection n{.a, .b} , so write the map out): MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.member_no <= 3 RETURN {no: m.member_no, name: m.name, faction: m.faction} AS member, properties(m) AS all_properties
docs.title: Maps

docs.text: The generic form (conditions): MATCH (d:Document) RETURN d.title, CASE WHEN d.year < 2018 THEN 'early' WHEN d.year < 2023 THEN 'middle' ELSE 'recent' END AS era ORDER BY d.year LIMIT 10 The simple form (one value against several): MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no, CASE m.role WHEN 'instructor' THEN 'teaches' WHEN 'administrator' THEN 'runs the club' ELSE 'trains' END AS does ORDER BY m.member_no LIMIT 5
docs.title: CASE

docs.text: Strings: RETURN toUpper('graph') AS up, toLower('GRAPH') AS low, trim(' x ') AS trim, ltrim(' x') AS ltrim, rtrim('x ') AS rtrim, replace('a-b-c', '-', '+') AS replace, substring('openCypher', 4) AS sub, substring('openCypher', 0, 4) AS sub2, left('openCypher', 4) AS left, right('openCypher', 6) AS right, split('a,b,c', ',') AS split, reverse('abc') AS rev, size('hello') AS size Numbers: RETURN abs(-3) AS abs, ceil(1.2) AS ceil, floor(1.8) AS floor, round(2.5) AS round, round(3.14159, 2) AS round2, round(2.5, 0, 'HALF_EVEN') AS banker, sign(-4) AS sign, sqrt(16) AS sqrt, exp(1) AS exp, log(e()) AS log, log10(1000) AS log10 Trigonometry and constants: RETURN pi() AS pi, e() AS e, sin(pi() / 2) AS sin, cos(0) AS cos, tan(0) AS tan, asin(1) AS asin, acos(1) AS acos, atan(1) AS atan, atan2(1, 1) AS atan2, degrees(pi()) AS degrees, radians(180) AS radians Conversions: RETURN toInteger('42') AS i, toInteger(3.9) AS trunc, toFloat('2.5') AS f, toBoolean('true') AS b, toString(12) AS s, toString(true) AS s2, toInteger('nope') AS bad Others: coalesce , timestamp (milliseconds since 1970), randomUUID and rand (0 to 1): RETURN coalesce(null, null, 'third') AS first_non_null, timestamp() AS now_ms, randomUUID() AS uuid, rand() AS random
docs.title: Functions

docs.text: All nodes with a label, and inline property maps: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m ORDER BY m.member_no LIMIT 5 MATCH (m:Member {faction: 'Officer', role: 'member'}) RETURN m.member_no, m.name ORDER BY m.member_no Any node, with a label test in WHERE : MATCH (n) WHERE n:Document AND n.year = 2015 RETURN labels(n) AS labels, n.title Several labels at once ( :A:B ): no sample node has two, so this returns nothing, but it shows the syntax in both places: MATCH (n:Member:Person) RETURN n UNION MATCH (n) WHERE n:Member:Document RETURN n Relationship directions: outgoing, incoming, either way, and anonymous relationships: MATCH (d:Document {title: 'Pattern matching, part 2'})-[:CITES]->(cited) RETURN 'cites' AS dir, cited.title AS title UNION ALL MATCH (d:Document {title: 'Pattern matching, part 2'})<-[:CITES]-(citing) RETURN 'cited by' AS dir, citing.title AS title MATCH (:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(friend) RETURN friend.member_no ORDER BY friend.member_no MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 34})--(b) RETURN count(b) AS either, size([(a)-->(x) | x]) AS out, size([(a)<--(x) | x]) AS in A relationship variable, its type and properties, and type alternatives [:A|B] : MATCH (a)-[r:FRIENDS_WITH|CITES]->(b) RETURN type(r) AS type, count(*) AS n MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[r:FRIENDS_WITH]->(b) RETURN r, startNode(r).name AS from, endNode(r).name AS to LIMIT 3 Longer chains: friends of friends that are not direct friends: MATCH (me:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(fof) WHERE fof <> me AND NOT (me)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(fof) RETURN DISTINCT fof.member_no AS suggestion ORDER BY suggestion Cycles: every friendship triangle, each once: MATCH (a:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(b:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(c:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(a) WHERE a.member_no < b.member_no < c.member_no RETURN a.member_no, b.member_no, c.member_no ORDER BY a.member_no, b.member_no, c.member_no Several pattern parts separated by commas, sharing a node: MATCH (hi:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(x), (x)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(john:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN x.member_no AS friend_of_both, x.faction Several MATCH clauses in a row: MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1}) MATCH (b:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN a.name, b.name, (a)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(b) AS are_friends
docs.title: MATCH and patterns

docs.text: Exactly 2 hops ( *2 ), a range ( *1..2 ), at most ( *..2 ), and at least ( *2.. , capped by the server): MATCH (:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*2]-(m) RETURN DISTINCT m.member_no ORDER BY m.member_no MATCH (:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*1..2]-(m) RETURN count(DISTINCT m) AS within_two_hops MATCH (:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*..2]-(m) RETURN count(DISTINCT m) AS within_two_hops MATCH (d:Document {title: 'Variable-length paths, part 2'})-[:CITES*3..]->(old) RETURN DISTINCT old.title, old.year ORDER BY old.year LIMIT 5 Any number of hops ( * ) along the citations, with a path variable, and the path functions: MATCH p = (d:Document {title: 'Variable-length paths, part 2'})-[:CITES*]->(old:Document {year: 2015}) RETURN p, length(p) AS hops, [n IN nodes(p) | n.year] AS years, [r IN relationships(p) | type(r)] AS types ORDER BY hops LIMIT 3 A path variable on a fixed-length pattern, and a relationship-list variable on a variable-length one: MATCH p = (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->(b)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->(c) RETURN p, length(p) AS len LIMIT 5 MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[rs:FRIENDS_WITH*2]-(c:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN [r IN rs | [startNode(r).member_no, endNode(r).member_no]] AS steps
docs.title: Variable-length patterns and paths

docs.text: shortestPath() (one) and allShortestPaths() (every one of the shortest length): MATCH p = shortestPath((a:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*]-(b:Member {member_no: 26})) RETURN p, length(p) AS hops, [n IN nodes(p) | n.member_no] AS via MATCH p = allShortestPaths((a:Member {member_no: 17})-[:FRIENDS_WITH*]-(b:Member {member_no: 26})) RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.member_no] AS via ORDER BY via With a hop limit, and following direction: MATCH p = shortestPath((a:Document {title: 'Variable-length paths, part 2'})-[:CITES*..10]->(b:Document {year: 2015})) RETURN b.title, length(p) AS hops ORDER BY hops, b.title
docs.title: Shortest paths

docs.text: Keeps the row, with nulls, when the pattern isn't found: the first paper cites nothing: MATCH (d:Document) WHERE d.year <= 2016 OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:CITES]->(c:Document) RETURN d.title, d.year, count(c) AS cites, collect(c.title) AS titles ORDER BY d.year, d.title MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 12}) OPTIONAL MATCH (m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f:Member) WHERE f.member_no > 1 RETURN m.member_no, f.member_no AS other_friend
docs.title: OPTIONAL MATCH

docs.text: A pattern as a condition, and its negation: MATCH (m:Member) WHERE (m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(:Member {member_no: 1}) AND (m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN m.member_no AS friend_of_both_leaders MATCH (d:Document) WHERE NOT (d)<-[:CITES]-() RETURN d.title AS never_cited, d.year ORDER BY d.year DESC LIMIT 10 EXISTS { pattern } , with or without a WHERE : MATCH (d:Document) WHERE EXISTS { (d)-[:CITES]->(other:Document) WHERE other.topic <> d.topic } RETURN d.title AS cites_another_topic, d.topic ORDER BY d.title Pattern comprehensions: a list built from a pattern, per row: MATCH (m:Member) WHERE m.member_no IN [1, 34] RETURN m.name, [(m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WHERE f.faction <> m.faction | f.member_no] AS friends_across_the_split Counting with one (the engine has no COUNT { } subquery): MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no, size([(m)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) | f]) AS friends ORDER BY friends DESC LIMIT 5
docs.title: Pattern predicates, EXISTS and pattern comprehensions

docs.text: Passing values on, filtering after an aggregate (like SQL's HAVING ): MATCH (m:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WITH m, count(f) AS friends WHERE friends >= 10 RETURN m.member_no, m.name, friends ORDER BY friends DESC ORDER BY and LIMIT inside WITH , before matching on: MATCH (d:Document) WITH d ORDER BY d.year DESC, d.title LIMIT 1 MATCH (d)-[:CITES]->(c) RETURN d.title AS newest, collect(c.title) AS it_cites WITH DISTINCT , and WITH * (keep every variable, add more): MATCH (d:Document) WITH DISTINCT d.topic AS topic RETURN topic ORDER BY topic MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(b) WITH *, b.member_no * 10 AS score RETURN a.member_no, b.member_no, score ORDER BY score LIMIT 3 Chaining several WITH stages: MATCH (d:Document) WITH d.topic AS topic, min(d.year) AS first, max(d.year) AS last WITH topic, last - first AS span WHERE span > 5 RETURN topic, span ORDER BY topic
docs.title: WITH

docs.text: RETURN * , RETURN DISTINCT , aliases, expressions: MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 34}) RETURN * MATCH (m:Member) RETURN DISTINCT m.faction AS faction, m.role AS role ORDER BY faction, role Several sort keys, ascending and descending ( ASC , ASCENDING , DESC , DESCENDING ): MATCH (d:Document) RETURN d.topic, d.year, d.title ORDER BY d.topic ASCENDING, d.year DESC LIMIT 8 Paging with SKIP and LIMIT , including expressions: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no ORDER BY m.member_no SKIP 10 LIMIT 5 MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no ORDER BY m.member_no SKIP $page * $size LIMIT $size {"page": 2, "size": 5} Nulls sort last when ascending (first when descending): UNWIND [3, null, 1, 2] AS x RETURN x ORDER BY x
docs.title: RETURN, ORDER BY, SKIP and LIMIT

docs.text: count(*) , count(expr) (skips nulls), count(DISTINCT ...) ; the other columns are the grouping keys: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.faction AS faction, count(*) AS members, count(DISTINCT m.role) AS roles ORDER BY faction UNWIND [1, null, 2, 2] AS x RETURN count(*) AS rows, count(x) AS values, count(DISTINCT x) AS distinct_values sum , avg , min , max : MATCH (d:Document) RETURN d.topic, sum(d.year) AS sum, avg(d.year) AS avg, min(d.year) AS min, max(d.title) AS last_title ORDER BY d.topic collect and collect(DISTINCT ...) : MATCH (m:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WHERE m.member_no IN [1, 34] RETURN m.name, collect(f.member_no) AS friends, collect(DISTINCT f.faction) AS factions Statistics: stDev (sample), stDevP (population), percentileCont (interpolated), percentileDisc (an actual value): MATCH (m:Member)-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) WITH m, count(f) AS degree RETURN stDev(degree) AS stdev, stDevP(degree) AS stdevp, percentileCont(degree, 0.5) AS median, percentileDisc(degree, 0.9) AS p90, avg(degree) AS mean Aggregates inside expressions, and aggregating a whole graph to one row: MATCH (d:Document) RETURN count(*) AS papers, max(d.year) - min(d.year) + 1 AS years, round(toFloat(count(*)) / 4, 1) AS per_topic
docs.title: Aggregation

docs.text: A list into rows, nested UNWIND s, and range() : UNWIND ['a', 'b'] AS letter UNWIND range(1, 3) AS n RETURN letter + toString(n) AS cell From a parameter, then matching on each value: UNWIND $members AS no MATCH (m:Member {member_no: no}) RETURN no, m.name, m.faction {"members": [1, 9, 34]} A collected list back into rows: MATCH (d:Document {topic: 'vector retrieval'}) WITH collect(d) AS docs UNWIND docs[0..3] AS d RETURN d.title An empty list gives no rows: UNWIND [] AS x RETURN x
docs.title: UNWIND

docs.text: UNION removes duplicate rows, UNION ALL keeps them; the column names must match: MATCH (m:Member {role: 'instructor'}) RETURN m.name AS name UNION MATCH (m:Member {role: 'administrator'}) RETURN m.name AS name UNION MATCH (m:Member {role: 'instructor'}) RETURN m.name AS name RETURN 1 AS x UNION ALL RETURN 1 AS x UNION ALL RETURN 2 AS x
docs.title: UNION

docs.text: Values of every JSON type, used in a pattern and in expressions: MATCH (m:Member {faction: $faction}) WHERE m.member_no IN $numbers AND m.name STARTS WITH $prefix RETURN m.member_no, m.name, $flag AS flag, $settings.colour AS colour {"faction": "Mr. Hi", "numbers": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 20], "prefix": "Member", "flag": true, "settings": {"colour": "blue"}} Finding a node by its id, as the console's Expand neighbours does (take an id from any answer): MATCH (a)-[r]-(b) WHERE id(a) = $id RETURN a, r, b {"id": "paste an id here"}
docs.title: Parameters

docs.text: A node's id, labels, keys and properties, and a relationship's type and ends: MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 1})-[r:FRIENDS_WITH]->(b:Member {member_no: 2}) RETURN id(a) AS id, elementId(a) AS element_id, labels(a) AS labels, keys(a) AS keys, properties(a) AS props, type(r) AS type, id(startNode(r)) = id(a) AS starts_at_a, endNode(r).name AS ends_at degree() : all relationships, or one direction only: MATCH (m:Member) RETURN m.member_no, degree(m) AS all, degree(m, 'out') AS out, degree(m, 'in') AS in ORDER BY all DESC LIMIT 5 exists(property) (from older openCypher; IS NOT NULL is the modern form): MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) RETURN exists(m.name) AS has_name, exists(m.nickname) AS has_nickname length() of a path and size() of a list or string: MATCH p = (:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->()-[:FRIENDS_WITH]->() RETURN length(p) AS path, size(nodes(p)) AS nodes, size('abc') AS string LIMIT 1
docs.title: Graph functions

docs.text: These run in graph-tool over the whole graph. YIELD names the columns, AS renames them, and a WHERE after YIELD filters them. PageRank, on the friendships only, both directions: CALL gt.pageRank({direction: 'BOTH', relationshipTypes: ['FRIENDS_WITH'], dampingFactor: 0.85}) YIELD node, score AS rank WHERE node:Member RETURN node.member_no, node.name, round(rank, 4) AS rank ORDER BY rank DESC LIMIT 5 The most cited papers by PageRank (direction follows the citations): CALL gt.pageRank({relationshipTypes: ['CITES'], maxIterations: 100, tolerance: 0.000001}) YIELD node, score WHERE node:Document RETURN node.title, node.year, round(score, 4) AS score ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 5 Connected components: CALL gt.connectedComponents() YIELD node, componentId RETURN componentId, labels(node)[0] AS label, count(*) AS size ORDER BY size DESC Label propagation ( gt.peerPressure ), its clusters set against the club's two factions: CALL gt.peerPressure({relationshipTypes: ['FRIENDS_WITH'], maxIterations: 30}) YIELD node, cluster WITH node, cluster WHERE node:Member RETURN cluster, node.faction AS faction, count(*) AS members ORDER BY cluster, faction A shortest path from a procedure, with matched nodes as its arguments: MATCH (a:Member {member_no: 17}), (b:Member {member_no: 26}) CALL gt.shortestPath(a, b, {direction: 'BOTH', relationshipTypes: ['FRIENDS_WITH']}) YIELD path, totalCost RETURN path, totalCost, [n IN nodes(path) | n.member_no] AS via
docs.title: Graph algorithm procedures

docs.text: The parameter q is a 16-number stand-in for the embedding of a question about vector retrieval (the centre of the sample's "vector retrieval" topic); it is the same under each query here. The k most similar papers (a nearest-neighbour search in Cassandra): CALL vector.search('Document', 'embedding', $q, 5) YIELD node, score RETURN node.title AS title, node.topic AS topic, round(score, 4) AS score {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} With a filter on an indexed field, applied inside Cassandra: CALL vector.search('Document', 'embedding', $q, 3, {topic: 'query languages'}) YIELD node, score RETURN node.title AS title, round(score, 4) AS score {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} Vector search, then the graph: what the best matches cite: CALL vector.search('Document', 'embedding', $q, 3) YIELD node, score MATCH (node)-[:CITES*1..2]->(src:Document) RETURN src.title AS cited, max(round(score, 4)) AS relevance ORDER BY relevance DESC, cited LIMIT 5 {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} The graph, then similarity: the similarity functions score vectors already in hand ( vector.cosine , vector.dot_product , vector.euclidean , each from 0 to 1): MATCH (d:Document) WITH d ORDER BY d.year DESC LIMIT 1 MATCH (d)-[:CITES*1..3]->(c:Document) RETURN DISTINCT c.title AS title, round(vector.cosine(c.embedding, $q), 4) AS cosine, round(vector.dot_product(c.embedding, $q), 4) AS dot, round(vector.euclidean(c.embedding, $q), 4) AS euclidean ORDER BY cosine DESC LIMIT 5 {"q": [-0.097498, -0.030158, 0.179123, 0.070401, -0.126774, -0.271176, -0.147528, 0.345993, -0.228961, 0.069361, 0.12087, -0.422174, 0.013737, 0.370172, -0.570844, -0.091135]} Two papers compared with each other: MATCH (a:Document {title: 'Leader leases, part 1'}), (b:Document) WHERE b <> a RETURN b.title, b.topic, round(vector.cosine(a.embedding, b.embedding), 4) AS similarity ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT 5
docs.title: Vector search

docs.text: The plan, not the answer: where each pattern starts and how its start nodes are found. The console's Explain button adds the EXPLAIN for you. EXPLAIN MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1})-[:FRIENDS_WITH]-(f) RETURN f.name EXPLAIN of a write is a read, so the console accepts it: EXPLAIN MATCH (m:Member {member_no: 1}) SET m.role = 'instructor' RETURN m
docs.title: EXPLAIN

docs.text: Not in the console , which refuses writes: send these to POST /opencypher with a key that may write, for example curl -s -X POST 127.0.0.1:5050/opencypher -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"query": "CREATE (p:Person {name: $name}) RETURN p", "params": {"name": "Catalogue Ann"}}' They use the data model's Person / KNOWS types, with names starting Catalogue , and run in order; the last one removes everything they made. In the console, Explain shows each one's plan. CREATE : a node, a path, and a relationship between nodes already there: CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann', address: '1 First St'}) RETURN p CREATE (b:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'})-[k:KNOWS {since: 2020}]->(c:Person {name: 'Catalogue Cat'}) RETURN b, k, c MATCH (a:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}), (b:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'}) CREATE (a)-[k:KNOWS {since: 2015}]->(b) RETURN a, k, b MERGE : find or create, with ON CREATE SET and ON MATCH SET (run it twice to see both): MERGE (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Dan'}) ON CREATE SET p.address = 'created' ON MATCH SET p.address = 'matched' RETURN p.name, p.address MATCH (a:Person {name: 'Catalogue Dan'}), (b:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) MERGE (a)-[k:KNOWS]->(b) ON CREATE SET k.since = 2024 RETURN k.since Many at once, from a parameter: UNWIND $people AS person MERGE (p:Person {name: person.name}) SET p.address = person.address RETURN count(p) AS merged {"people": [{"name": "Catalogue Eve", "address": "5 Fifth St"}, {"name": "Catalogue Fay", "address": "6 Sixth St"}]} SET : one property, several properties from a map ( += adds, = replaces them all), and a label: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) SET p.address = '2 Second St' RETURN p MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'}) SET p += {address: '3 Third St'} RETURN properties(p) MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Cat'}) SET p = {name: 'Catalogue Cat', address: '4 Fourth St'} RETURN properties(p) MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) SET p:Member RETURN labels(p) REMOVE : a property and a label: MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'}) REMOVE p.address, p:Member RETURN p.address, labels(p) DELETE a relationship, then DETACH DELETE the nodes with their relationships: MATCH (:Person {name: 'Catalogue Ann'})-[k:KNOWS]->(:Person {name: 'Catalogue Bob'}) DELETE k MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.name STARTS WITH 'Catalogue' DETACH DELETE p
docs.title: Writes
